title: Human Reference Atlas 3D reference organs (Visible Human Female) in the SpinDrift app frame

axes.x: +x = body's left, so the body's right is -x
axes.y: up; the lowest skin vertex is y = 0

source_frame.axes: metres, y up, +x body's left, +z anterior (see laterality_evidence)

hra_to_app.why: The HRA VHFemale body frame already has the app's axes (metres, y up, +z anterior, body's right at -x), so no rotation or scaling is applied. Its origin is near mid-body (the skin spans y from -0.793 m to +0.865 m), so y is shifted by the lowest skin vertex to put the soles at y = 0. x and z keep the HRA origin.

head_bbox_app.method: Head = the skin vertices with y >= the chin point's y; min, max, center and size of their bounding box. Chin point: on the skin's anterior midline profile (rays along -z in the plane x = brain centroid x, every 1 mm in y, first skin hit; Moller-Trumbore), the point between the suprasternal notch and the nose tip lying farthest in front of the straight line joining them, i.e. the chin's lower corner where the underside of the chin turns into its front. Nose tip = most anterior profile point from 0.10 m below to 0.06 m above the brain's lowest point; suprasternal notch = most posterior profile point within 0.25 m below the nose tip. The landmark names say what the construction finds on this mesh; the HRA skin itself has no landmarks. The cut is horizontal (app frame), so the bounding box also holds the upper back of the neck at chin height; the ears are included.

cross_checks.ccf_global_placements: Each organ's CCF global placement relative to #VHFemale (graph.jsonld) has no rotation, unit scale, and a translation equal to the GLB bounding-box minimum in mm (max difference per model in models.*.placement).

united_female.citation: Browne, Kristen, and Heidi Schlehlein. 2026. *3D Reference Organ Set for Female, v1.10*. https://doi.org/10.48539/HBM637.DWBM.744. Accessed on June 15, 2026.
united_female.note: In the HRA united female assembly the roots of the models used here carry no transform except VH_F_skin, which carries a rotation and scale (linear part not the identity) and a translation of [-349.85, 579.915, -251.994] mm; through those transforms the accessor bounds of its 1 meshes give the standalone file's bounding box to within 0.00012 mm, so the united file stores the same geometry in another local frame. The HRA API scene, used for the app frame, places every one of them with the identity, so the difference is reported, not applied.

load.note: All files are uncompressed GLB (no Draco, no meshopt); three.js GLTFLoader alone loads them. This set has no optional model: the HRA female blood vasculature (17875996 bytes) is not part of it and was not downloaded; only its GLB JSON chunk was read (HTTP range requests), for the forearm search.

materials: The app replaces each file material with a plain MeshStandardMaterial that keeps the file's base colour, roughness and metalness; the skin gets a translucent neutral material. The files hold no textures.

skin.description: This reference organ, Skin-female (https://humanatlas.io/3d-reference-library) was created using data from the Visible Human Dataset, provided by the National Library of Medicine (Spitzer and Whitlock 2002). In version v1.3, the torso of the skin model was moved up from previous editions to incorporate the clavicles and other anatomy for the breast. It was also adjusted to add space for the triceps surae and the ankle bones for the eventual addition of the triceps surae muscles and landmark organs. In v2.3, the head was adjusted to be more like the original skin of the Visible Human Female, to make space for the mouth 3D object and landmarks.

brain.description: This reference organ, Brain-female (https://humanatlas.io/3d-reference-library) was created using data from the Allen brain reference atlas (Ding et al. 2016). The 141 anatomical structures were mirrored to arrive at a whole human brain (as intended) and resized to fit the Visible Human Male and Female bodies (Spitzer et al. 1996; Ackerman 1998; Spitzer and Whitlock 2002). In version v1.3, an update in licensing occurred; this brain model is now licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Ding et al. 2016 was used to inform the creation of this model.

mounts.frame: app (metres, y up, feet at y = 0, +z anterior, body's right = -x)

scalp_right_precentral_gyrus.method: Precentral gyrus mesh chosen by the HRA crosswalk ID UBERON:0002703 ('precentral gyrus' on EBI OLS); of its two meshes, the one at -x (body's right). Gyrus centroid G = area-weighted mean of its triangle centroids. Grid centre C = closest point of the skin mesh (head region) to G; normal = the skin file's vertex normals interpolated at C (barycentric), oriented away from G. Grid axes: t1 = the gyrus' principal axis (area-weighted PCA of its triangles) projected on the tangent plane at C, pointing superior; t2 = n x t1, pointing anterior. Each of the 9 points: the target C + 0.025 m (i t1 + j t2) is projected onto the scalp by a ray along -n from 0.08 m outside (Moller-Trumbore on the skin triangles); the normal there is interpolated the same way. Underlying structure: first brain mesh hit by a ray from each point along -normal.

target_mesh.label_conflict: The HRA brain file labels this mesh 'Allen_primary_motor_cortex_L' and its hemisphere 'left cerebral hemisphere', yet it lies at -x, which is the body's right in the HRA VHFemale frame (right kidney, right lung with its middle lobe, and the heart's right atrium are at -x; the left ventricle is at +x). HRA built this brain by mirroring one Allen hemisphere, so the two sides are mirror copies and the geometry cannot settle laterality. The body frame is used; the file label is reported, not changed.

file_label_R_alternative.note: The same construction for 'Allen_primary_motor_cortex_R' (HRA file label R), which lies at +x = body's left.

chest_over_heart.method: Heart centroid H = area-weighted mean of the triangle centroids of all heart meshes (HRA heart v1.3). Ray from H along +z (anterior in the HRA body frame); the first skin intersection (Moller-Trumbore) is the mount point. Normal = the skin file's vertex normals interpolated at the hit, oriented outward (+z side).

evidence.blood_vasculature_source: GLB JSON chunk of https://cdn.humanatlas.io/digital-objects/ref-organ/blood-vasculature-female/v1.3/assets/3d-vh-f-blood-vasculature.glb (https://purl.humanatlas.io/ref-organ/blood-vasculature-female/v1.3#primary, 17875996 bytes, not downloaded), read by HTTP range requests: the names of its 110 mesh nodes, and the x extent from the POSITION accessor bounds through the node transforms (its HRA scene transform is the identity, and the app frame shifts only y)

forearm_right_volar.reason: No upper-limb bone, vessel or landmark exists in the HRA female set (none of the reference organs, blood vasculature nodes or united female assembly nodes match; the vasculature stays within the trunk and head). The skin alone has no landmarks, so no point is given.
